replies.author: Ogrey
replies.body: The concept of it is good enough for a map, but overall I can't say I like it much nor the way it was executed, which is poorly. All of the blocks were placed in a way that they severely clash with eachother, not offering any positive aesthetical value to the map. With every morsel of glowstone you clam down on the ground that doesn't follow any organized pattern, plus the blockyness of the few structures scattered through the map and randomness in which an area entirely constituted of quartz suddenly changes to a few tiles of stained clay with glass just... doesn't blend in quite smoothly. My suggestion? Rid of the pedestrian look the map withholds. You can stick to your current block palette, but you must know how to apply it to the map in order to make it look better. Try coming up with a better set of structures, because those you've built in the cubic areas (both the spawn and middle zones) are... not very fitting to the rest of the map. Something a bit more strategical, maybe? Thicken up the flooring and (maybe) walls, and the glass surrounding the spawnpoint...? I don't think that fits very well in there...
